clue.text: Kick the bucket, cutting end of lobster's tail off

indicators.note: cutting says one piece slices into the middle of another

parts.note: to kick the bucket is slang for to die, to decease

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A grim instruction about dying while a lobster loses its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' puts R, the last letter of 'lobster's', into DECEASE. 'tail off' looks like part of the lobster scene but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail off is to dwindle or lessen gradually, a synonym of the verb meaning to lessen.

clue.text: Pudding lacks a bit of sauce — it's very dry

indicators.note: lacks tells us a letter is missing from the word

parts.note: dessert is the pudding course of a meal

indicators.note: a bit of picks out the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A pudding with too little sauce is very dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of' gives S from 'sauce'; 'lacks' removes one S from DESSERT.
explanation.definitionFit: An arid wilderness such as the Sahara is the very dry place described.

clue.text: Mark fixes Beetle car

indicators.note: fixes in the sense of rigs or repairs, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark repairs a Volkswagen Beetle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixes' rearranges BEETLE CAR. 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark an occasion is to commemorate it, a synonym of the verb meaning honour festively.

clue.text: Last text remembered to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Only part of the final text was remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to an extent' says only part of 'text remembered' is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The extreme point of something is its furthest or final one, so last is a synonym.

clue.text: Carol sits on top of saucepan and spills the beans

indicators.note: sits on places the first piece above the second in a down answer

parts.note: to carol is to sing

indicators.note: top of picks out the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone named Carol perches on a saucepan and spills beans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of' gives S from 'saucepan'. 'Carol' looks like a name but is a verb, and 'spills the beans' is slang for confessing.
explanation.definitionFit: To sing, in criminal slang, is to inform or confess, just as spilling the beans means revealing secrets.

clue.text: Matches could make you squeal

indicators.note: could make you hints that the letters of the next word can be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Losing a match might make you squeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make you' signals rearranging the letters of SQUEAL. 'Matches' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To match something is to be its equal, so matches and equals are synonymous verbs.

clue.text: Tests grills

definitions.meaning: tests as a noun, sets of questions to check knowledge
grills as a verb, questions intensely

explanation.definitionFit: Short tests of knowledge, and also the verb meaning to interrogate someone closely.

clue.text: A story keeps Victoria initially awake

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a story can mean a lie, a falsehood

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A bedtime story keeps young Victoria awake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives V from 'Victoria'; 'keeps' puts it inside LIE, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Being awake means being lively and alert, so the word for living and alert fits.

clue.text: Afters set out — that's most kind

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert, also called a sweet

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Laying out dessert is the kindest gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET into EST. AFTERS is British slang for the dessert course.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet can mean kind or thoughtful, so the superlative means most kind.

clue.text: Force Noel to get involved in depravity

indicators.note: in places the tangled letters inside the other word

parts.note: vice is depravity or wickedness

indicators.note: to get involved suggests the letters become tangled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Noel is drawn into corruption by force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get involved' signals the anagram of the name, and 'in' the insertion; Noel is not a person in the scene but raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical force used to harm is the essence of violent behaviour, a close synonym.

clue.text: Rent almost vast — I have to formally offend?

parts.note: rent, as a past participle of rend, means torn or split

indicators.note: almost tells us to drop the final letter of the synonym

parts.note: vast means immense, infinite
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A complaint that the rent is almost unbearably high, voiced with offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of the synonym for vast. The definition is an example: 'to formally offend' itself puts an adverb between 'to' and the verb, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an example of the construction, with an adverb wedged between 'to' and its verb.

clue.text: They get ready without asking

parts.note: ready is slang for cash, so people who take money without asking are thieves

explanation.definitionFit: Thieves who take money (ready cash) without permission are described here.

clue.text: Zeal? It's foreign for this type

definitions.text: Zeal? It's foreign for this type

indicators.note: foreign suggests the letters are strange and out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Enthusiasm is alien to an idle sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges ZEAL and ITS. The whole clue also defines: zeal is foreign to the most idle type.
explanation.definitionFit: The most idle sort of person is the one for whom enthusiasm is utterly alien.

clue.text: Trader who may call girl nasty names

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who phones a girl and calls her nasty names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges SAL and NAMES. The surface's 'call girl' is a red herring: 'call' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling seller calls on customers at their homes to sell goods.

clue.text: Bad behaviour from woman, almost kissing boss

indicators.note: kissing means touching, so the two pieces sit next to each other
almost tells us to drop the final letter

parts.note: a miss is a young woman
a chief is a boss

explanation.surface: A woman is caught kissing her boss, which is bad behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts MISS to MIS; 'kissing' sets it right against CHIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief is naughty or troublesome conduct, especially by children.

clue.text: Parts left off playground items

indicators.note: off tells us to take the letter away from the word

parts.note: slides are typical items of playground equipment

explanation.surface: Parts of the playground equipment have been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes L from SLIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sides are parts or sections of something, as in the sides of an argument.

clue.text: Carried out evil deed without resistance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word surrounds the rest
out suggests the letters are disordered and rearranged

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone committed a wicked act without meeting any opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals the anagram of 'evil'; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. 'Carried out' reads as one phrase, but only 'Carried' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are carried to someone are brought to them, a synonym in the sense of conveyed.

clue.text: Gives tests about identification

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: proves can mean tests, as in proving ground

explanation.surface: An official runs checks on identity papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals that the word for tests wraps round the abbreviation; 'Gives' is a verb, matching the answer's form.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide something is to supply or give it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Grasses small animal brought over

indicators.note: brought over suggests turning the pieces back to front

parts.note: a deer is an animal

explanation.surface: Grass is gathered and a small creature carried across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' turns SDEER back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are tall grasses that grow in wet places, so they are a type of grass.

clue.text: Silicone at first put down crack

indicators.note: at first picks out the opening letter of the preceding word

parts.note: an animal put down is killed

explanation.surface: Silicone was applied first to fill a crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives S from 'Silicone'. 'crack' is an adjective, as in a crack shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Crack, as an adjective, means expert or first-rate, as in a crack marksman.

clue.text: Doctor I stayed with left regularly

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A patient says they stayed with the doctor and then left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb meaning tamper: it rearranges I STAYED plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something steadily means doing it at an even, regular pace.

clue.text: Madden tailor with small orders

indicators.note: to tailor is to alter, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A tailor is driven mad by small orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailor' is a verb meaning alter: it rearranges MADDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Demands are firm orders or requests insisted on, a synonym of the plural noun.

clue.text: Conservative changed roles to become more intimate

indicators.note: changed suggests the letters are swapped around

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician changed roles to get closer to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges ROLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A closer friend is a more intimate one, the comparative of near or dear.

clue.text: Japan very rash in conflicts

indicators.note: conflicts suggests the letters clash and end up jumbled

explanation.surface: Japan behaved very rashly in its wars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conflicts' rearranges RASH IN into ARNISH. Japan here is a verb, to coat with hard glossy lacquer, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To japan is to coat with a hard black lacquer, much as one would apply a gloss coat.

clue.text: Bottom of plant getting in rake's way

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so a letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man, a roue

indicators.note: bottom of picks out the last letter of the following word in a down clue

explanation.surface: A garden plant growing in the way of a rake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom of' gives T from 'plant'; 'getting in' puts it into ROUE. The garden 'rake' is a man of loose morals.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a way or course taken from one place to another.

clue.text: Dismissal concerning last in team on cricket ground

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: last in picks out the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the Oval is a London cricket ground

explanation.surface: A cricketer is dismissed as the last man in at a London ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last in' gives M, the final letter of 'team'. THE OVAL is a famous London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Removal from office is a dismissal, a synonym in the sense of being sacked.

clue.text: Nelson perhaps left house for relation

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letters go away

parts.note: Horatio Nelson was the famous British admiral, so Horatio is an example of a Nelson

explanation.surface: Admiral Nelson moved out of his house to stay with a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes HO from HORATIO. 'relation' is not family here but a proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is the numerical relation between two quantities.

clue.text: They're said to be both clean and dirty

definitions.text: They're said to be both clean and dirty

parts.words: They're said to be both clean and dirty
parts.note: remarks that are said with an innocent meaning and a risque one at the same time

explanation.definitionFit: Phrases with two meanings, one innocent and one rude, fit this description exactly.

clue.text: Lays out swan, dead, in boat

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the boat

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a boat
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A dead swan is laid out in a boat, like a funeral scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. A pen is a female swan, and SS (steamship) is a standard crossword boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay out money is to spend it, so lays out is a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Think about arguments against ride when drunk

parts.note: cons are arguments against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: when drunk suggests the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Reasons not to drive when you are drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when drunk' rearranges RIDE into SIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider something is to think about it carefully, a straightforward synonym.
